name: Cards From Files
description: Proposes a proportionate, current set of cards for material a consumer already keeps in files, without writing them.
purpose: Give any consumer cards for the knowledge it already keeps in files, so recall starts from what is there instead of an empty store.
approach: Group the files that belong together, describe each group, and report which cards an edit has made stale.
out_of_scope: Writing cards (the card store does) and choosing which cards a task sees (the context assembler does).
milestones: 1. The selected builder's balanced score on the mixed pinned cases is at least that of every free topic builder, with a store far below one card per file (metric-cards-from-files).
knowledge: Code graphs and repository maps group code by its call and import structure without a model; topic cards a model writes add the names a person would search for. A card groups information on one topic from many files and sources; a card per file is an index of files, so per_file_symbols and the degenerate groupings are baselines for file finding and never builders to ship. The earlier selection of per_file_symbols came from the file-finding metric, whose cases have one needed file each and so favour a card per file by construction; that metric alone was ill-posed for this solution. Its cases are now one kind of a mixed set with topic cases and a store-size term, and the selection is back on llm_topic_cards until that one number decides.
measures_of_success: The files a piece of work needed are inside the first cards the fixed selector picks, with little noise and with files of more than one folder bundled when the task spans them, from a store of at most 0.25 cards per file, at a price per build a team would pay.
parameters: The model provider, for a builder that calls one.
inputs: A folder root, the list of files to read, and the cards already kept for it.
outputs: Cards in the card-store record shape (grouping, summary, keywords, files with their hashes), and the ids of kept cards whose files changed.
effects: Reads files; writes nothing (the caller writes through card-store).
usage_notes: Run it for a first index and after edits, passing the cards already kept so a builder skips covered files. The per-file builder is the free floor; a builder that calls a model has to buy its price in accuracy on the balanced score. The per-file builder is a baseline for finding one file, not a card builder. The free topic builders (cochange_topic_cards, import_graph_topic_cards, the replay of the saved paid build) are scored for free; docs/how-to/iterate-on-card-builders-without-repeating-model-calls.md says how to iterate before any paid run.
verdict_detail: import_graph_topic_cards leads cochange_topic_cards (cochange_topic_cards 0.582 against import_graph_topic_cards 0.609; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.492, 90 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards leads file_plus_topic_cards (file_plus_topic_cards 0.299 against import_graph_topic_cards 0.609; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.362, 201 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than llm_topic_cards (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=3.68e-05, 247 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than one_card (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=9.59e-70, 241 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than one_card_per_folder (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.63e-36, 166 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards leads per_file_symbols (per_file_symbols 0.299 against import_graph_topic_cards 0.609; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.492, 209 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than topic_cards_replay (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.00328, 225 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than two_cards (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=2.76e-70, 243 of 252 cases disagree)

name: Context Retriever
description: Cuts a corpus of files into units at natural boundaries and returns, for a request, the units that answer it best first within a token budget, or nothing when the request needs no context.
purpose: Show a task the context it needs and little else, for any consumer that keeps its knowledge in files.
approach: A fielded keyword index and a local meaning index fused by rank, a reranker over the best candidates that also reads the import graph and the history of changes, and a confidence gate that returns nothing when the corpus does not answer; every arm is scored on one balanced number.
out_of_scope: Writing cards (cards-from-files), storing them (card-store) and rendering a view for a consumer's loop (context-assembler, whose file_retrieval arm reads this seat).
milestones: Lexical, latent, dense, fused, reranked, learned and abstaining arms recorded on one number over file, topic, orientation and no-context requests; a model reranker prepared for a recorded cassette.
knowledge: Retrieval papers favour hybrid first stages and rerankers; code retrieval gains from structure (names, imports, co-change); a consumer's own labelled history is the best training data and stays with the consumer.
measures_of_success: The balanced score of metric-retrieve-context, which counts the recall of needed files within the budget, graded nDCG, the noise tokens shown, the size of the index, cost and time.
parameters: The budget in tokens, the corpus (a mapping of path to text) and an optional history of past changes; each arm's own settings are constructor arguments.
inputs: A request in words, and the files to retrieve from the first time.
outputs: Hits: unit id, file, first line, score, tokens and text, best first; an empty list means no context is needed.
effects: Reads the corpus it is given and keeps an index and a vector cache in the folder it is given; no network, and no model unless the arm is a model reranker.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("retrieve-context", {"query": "where is the retry delay computed?", "files": {"net.py": "def retry_delay(attempt): ..."}})` returns the hits.

description: What comes to mind for a request without being asked for: cards and facts the Subconscious offers because they are close to the request.

approach: Offer the closest items to a request, within a budget, and let the Mind take or ignore them.
milestones: 1. An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept (metric-offer-intuition).
measures_of_success: An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept.
outputs: Items offered to the Mind for a request.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Model Call
description: One narrow call: a prompt at a tier in, text out. The hub builds it on call-a-model, so a consumer that wants a one-question model needs no object of its own.
purpose: Ask a model a question at the tier that fits, for any consumer.
approach: Send the prompt to the provider the hub assembled for the tier and return the text.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-model-call has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-model-call has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-model-call chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Answer returned for the tier asked; cost and time recorded by the caller.
parameters: The provider, or the consumer's own object.
outputs: The text a model answers to the prompt.
effects: One call to a model provider, which costs what the provider charges or draws on the operator's subscription.
usage_notes: No hub arm: the consumer provides the object.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Vendor Model Caller
description: Plans, answers and lists models for one vendor, or for several through a router that steps to the next model when a provider fails.
purpose: Reach any model vendor through one interface, for any consumer that calls models.
approach: Wrap each vendor behind one interface and route each call to the provider that serves its model, with a fallback when it fails.
milestones: Arms for the main vendors and the Claude Code program, a router that fails over, and recorded failover and answer checks.
knowledge: Each vendor's SDK and the claude program have their own limits, listed beside the arm in the requirements table.
measures_of_success: A call is answered when the primary provider fails, and a failure that is not the provider's is raised. Vendor answer quality is measured on choose-a-model-tier (metric-vendor-answers).
parameters: Per vendor: key, base url, options and fallback models, all constructor arguments; nothing is read from the environment.
inputs: A model id and a prompt, or a planning request.
outputs: Text, a plan or a list of models.
effects: Network calls to the vendor; token totals are kept per calling thread.
usage_notes: Name no model: the seat's selected arm answers. Pass arms= to choose another.
verdict_detail: multi_provider is better than single_provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=7.63e-06, 18 of 30 cases disagree)

name: Model Tier Chooser
description: Picks, for each model tier, the provider and model that passes the most work per dollar on the same cases, counting prepaid credits as cost.
purpose: Choose the cheapest model that does the job at each tier, for any product that calls models.
approach: Rank each provider and model by passing work per cost on shared cases and the prices on file.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-choose-a-model-tier has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: The chosen model per tier passes the most work per dollar on shared cases.
parameters: bars: optional keyword arguments that set the quality bars.
inputs: tiers (tier name to candidate arms with cases run, cases passed and tokens), prices (rows from the price file), optional credits and defaults.
outputs: A mapping from each tier to the chosen provider and model.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Assembler
description: Builds the whole mind from configuration in one call: each seat gets its selected arm, and a seat that needs something from the consumer says exactly what to pass.
purpose: Give any consumer a working system from one line of configuration.
approach: Resolve each seat's selected arm and its needs, build what can be built and report what is still pending.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-assemble-the-whole has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The production stage of metric-assemble-the-whole has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-assemble-the-whole chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: End-to-end pass rate on a production consumer.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Integrity
description: Stays generic, claims match evidence, records match code. Audits the hub for consumer wording: the vendor-name branches in its own code, with how stale its research is and how much of it connects by configuration.
purpose: Keep the hub usable by any consumer, with no wording or settings of one product in it.
approach: Scan the hub for consumer-specific strings and keep prompts as data the consumer passes in.
milestones: 1. Consumer-specific strings found by the scan: none (metric-keep-it-generic).
measures_of_success: Consumer-specific strings found by scan (target 0).
outputs: Seats whose wording is data, whose arms are current and whose integrations are entries.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Role Understanding
description: Each part of the system knows what it is for, what it must hand on and what it must leave to the others, so that no part does another part's work or hides a failure of its own.
purpose: Give every part of an assembled system a clear role in the whole.
approach: State each part's role as data the part and the Assembler can read, and compare what a part does with the role it states.
milestones: 1. A part's behaviour matches the role the whole gives it (metric-role-understanding).
measures_of_success: A part's behaviour matches the role the whole gives it.
outputs: The role of each part, and whether its behaviour matches.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Model Plumbing
description: The one way every part asks a model: the tier chooser picks the model per tier, the model call asks it, and the vendor caller reaches the vendor and steps to the next provider when one fails.
purpose: Give every part one measured path to a model, so cost and failover are chosen once.
approach: Compose the Model Tier Chooser, Model Call and Vendor Model Caller, and measure each on shared cases.
milestones: 1. Every part asks a model through one measured path (metric-model-plumbing).
measures_of_success: Every part asks a model through one measured path.
outputs: An answer from the model that measured best for the tier, with a healthy vendor.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Science
description: Looks up what the world says now and returns it as observations a reader can cite, weighing papers and data rather than a single web page.
purpose: Support claims with sources a reader can check, for anyone who asks an AI a factual or research question.
approach: Search the strongest sources available and return their findings as citable observations.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-know-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-know-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-know-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-know-the-world chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Claims supported by sources; evidence weighed.
parameters: The search-backend a search arm needs, an optional API key and contact address for the scholarly service, and a timeout.
inputs: One query or a list of queries with an optional result limit and a freshness flag; or a page address with an optional focus, part and full flag.
outputs: One observation: title, link and snippet per hit, or the passages of a page that bear on a focus; a failure comes back as an observation of kind error, never a raised exception.
effects: Makes network requests to the scholarly service or the web and keeps a short cache; counts calls against a daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: Pass a query and read the hits of the returned observation, each with a link a reader can check.
verdict_detail: openalex_semantic leads openalex (openalex 0.05 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.019, 12 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic leads openalex_keywords (openalex_keywords 0.075 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0234, 13 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic leads openalex_keywords_model (openalex_keywords_model 0.075 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0234, 11 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic is better than openalex_semantic_and_web (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=6.2e-31, 150 of 150 cases disagree); openalex_semantic is better than web_research (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.12e-25, 150 of 150 cases disagree)

name: Web Search
description: One narrow call: a query in, a response of hits out. The hub ships thin adapters over open-source and hosted search services, and a consumer may provide its own.
purpose: Run a web search through any service, for any consumer that needs sources.
approach: Send the query to the chosen service and return hits with a title, a link and a snippet.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-search-backend has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The live stage of metric-search-backend has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-search-backend chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Result rows with a title, a link and a snippet for a query.
parameters: The service address or API key of the chosen arm, a timeout and an optional daily limit.
inputs: A query, a result limit and an optional instruction for a model-backed arm.
outputs: A response of hits (title, link, snippet, date, passages and their kind), an optional direct answer and the queries issued; raises SearchBackendError on failure.
effects: One network request per search to the chosen service, counted against the daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: The hub ships arms (searxng, serper, brave, tavily, gemini, provider) and a selector over them (hubofhubs.websearch.backends.select_search_backend). None is selected by default: no metric run exists yet, so a consumer names an arm in its selections or provides its own object.
verdict_detail: gemini is better than provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=1.1e-05, 22 of 40 cases disagree)

name: Tools
description: What the AI can use or do outside the system, grouped by category. A category is a solution and an integration is one of its implementations.
purpose: Let the AI use the best tool of each category without a product wiring each one.
approach: Choose the best integration of each category by measurement, and keep the long tail as registry entries.
milestones: 1. The best integration of each category is chosen by measurement (metric-use-tools).
measures_of_success: The best integration of each category is chosen by measurement.
outputs: The results of a tool the AI used, by category.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Personal Data Locations
description: Where a person keeps their own data, such as a calendar, a drive, a mailbox and notes, resolved as a fact about the setup rather than chosen by a metric contest.
purpose: Let the AI find a person's own data without each product asking again.
approach: Record each location once as setup, and hand it to the tools that need it.
milestones: 1. A location is declared once and every tool that needs it receives it (metric-personal-data-locations).
measures_of_success: A location is declared once and every tool that needs it receives it.
outputs: The locations of a person's data.
